**Test image key features:**
- Stem/branch junction with dark, blackened tissue
- Gray, dusty/powdery sporulation coating the entire stem
- White cottony mycelium visible at a wound/crack
- Classic "gray dust" appearance = Botrytis cinerea sporulation

**Reference comparison:**
- Gray_Mold: Bugwood_27 (leaf lesion), Bugwood_21 (fruit with white mold in crack), Bugwood_15 (microscopic spores) — the gray dusty sporulation on stem matches Botrytis
- Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers: Bugwood_7 shows dark stem lesion but NO gray dusty sporulation — not matching
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot: Bugwood_14 shows white cottony mycelium + black sclerotia, Bugwood_2 shows plant wilt — white mycelium present but the test image lacks sclerotia and has more gray dusty (not cottony) growth
- All other classes (Anthracnose, Bacterial_Canker, Bacterial_Speck, Bacterial_Wilt, Early_Blight, Late_Blight, Powdery_Mildew, Southern_Blight) show clearly different symptoms on leaves/fruit or whole plant wilt — none match the gray sporulation on stem

The defining feature is the **gray, dusty/powdery sporulation on darkened stem tissue** — the classic hallmark of *Botrytis cinerea* (Gray Mold). The white mycelium at the wound is consistent with early Botrytis colonization.
